title: Weather and zero-shot forecasting models: backtest results for GB electricity demand (part 1 of 2)
description:
The second study in a series testing off-the-shelf time-series foundation models (Chronos-2, Timestral-209M and TimesFM 2.5), used zero-shot, on Great Britain's national electricity demand a day ahead. It gives the models and a weekly-lag regression the same honestly timed weather: ECMWF open-data forecasts as public at the 09:30 issue time, with an ERA5 history.

Result (preregistered backtest, 960 days, 16 March 2024 to 31 October 2026). Weather cut mean daily error by 34% for the regression, 32% for Chronos-2, 23% for Timestral and 6% for TimesFM 2.5, each confirmed at a 5% study-wide error rate. Chronos-2 closed 62% of its gap to NESO's forecast. The models' edge over the regression found without weather largely disappears with it. The backtest overlaps the models' possible training data; a live window to 31 March 2027 is the descriptive check and will be reported in part 2.

The plan, code and inputs were frozen and hashed (tag weather-plan, 10 November 2026) before any model forecast demand with real weather; the backtest was scored once and passed every gate check. The archive contains the plan and lock, the results note (weather_study/RESULTS.md), the scored outputs and the power analyses. The weather-processing code is at github.com/AndyMoran/gb-weather-private. Contains BMRS data © Elexon Limited copyright and database right 2026. Supported by National Energy SO Open Data.
